article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 60% indica / 40% sativa
Genetics: Critical Mass
Breeder: Fast Buds
THC Content: Up to approximately 20%
CBD Content: Less than 1%
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Lemon, citrus, pine, earth, and floral notes
Flowering Time (Indoor): 10 weeks from seed to harvest
Outdoor Harvest Time: 10 weeks from germination
Indoor Yield: 350–550 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 50–150 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy

Critical Auto is built around a trait that has kept Critical-family cannabis relevant for years: efficiency. Rather than pursuing exotic coloration or dessert-style terpenes, Fast Buds concentrated on substantial flower production, uncomplicated cultivation, a short schedule, and a traditional citrus-pine aroma. The resulting plant can develop surprisingly massive colas for an autoflower, with tightly packed calyxes, golden pistils, and enough resin to make the branches visibly heavy by late bloom.

Its effect is equally practical, sitting between physical relaxation and a brighter creative headspace rather than pushing exclusively toward sedation. For marijuana growers who measure a cultivar by how much quality flower it can produce with relatively little drama, this automatic version makes a convincing case for keeping classic Critical genetics in modern gardens.
Genetics and Lineage

Fast Buds describes Critical Auto as its improved autoflowering interpretation of Critical Mass. On the current product page, however, the technical specification gives the genetics simply as “Critical Autoflower,” without naming a specific automatic parent or publishing a complete breeding formula. That distinction is worth preserving. Although Critical-family strains from other seed companies may provide more detailed parentage, those pedigrees should not automatically be assigned to Fast Buds’ version. The breeder-supported description is therefore a Critical Mass-derived autoflowering line developed specifically by Fast Buds.

The finished cultivar leans modestly toward the indica side at 60%, leaving enough sativa influence to explain its more animated mental effects and relatively vigorous growth. Automatic flowering allows the plant to transition into bloom according to maturity rather than waiting for shorter daylight hours. As with other widely used strain names, Critical Auto is available from multiple breeders, so genetics, potency, yield, and harvest figures can differ substantially. This profile refers specifically to Fast Buds rather than blending specifications from unrelated Critical Automatic lines.
Effects and Experience

Relaxation arrives early, but it does not necessarily shut down the mind. Fast Buds describes an immediate calming physical sensation accompanied by creativity, serenity, and enough motivation to remain socially or mentally engaged. In moderate amounts, the cultivar may fit a low-pressure evening with friends, gaming, music, movies, or creative hobbies better than an experience centered entirely on sleep. The body feels increasingly settled while the head can remain curious and imaginative, giving the high a more balanced progression than the 60% indica figure alone might suggest.

Larger doses change the character considerably. Fast Buds cautions that excessive consumption can push the experience toward a prolonged, dreamy state, which makes gradual dosing sensible for consumers with limited THC tolerance. With potency reaching roughly 20%, the flower is strong enough to produce substantial intoxication despite not competing with today’s highest-THC autos. Cannabis can slow reaction time, impair coordination and decision-making, and distort perception; the CDC therefore warns against driving while impaired by marijuana.
Medical Benefits

The combination of mental ease and physical relaxation may attract some medical marijuana consumers seeking a calmer evening experience. THC-rich cannabis is sometimes considered by patients managing persistent discomfort, appetite changes, stress, or difficulty relaxing, but Critical Auto itself has not been clinically established as a treatment for those conditions. Research on cannabis-based medicines is much broader than individual strain names . Reviews of cannabinoid-based medicines for chronic pain have found potential benefit for some patients, while also emphasizing adverse effects and the need for careful patient selection.

Fast Buds lists CBD below 1%, so this cultivar is predominantly THC-driven rather than a balanced CBD option. That makes personal sensitivity especially important. NIDA notes that larger amounts of THC-rich cannabis can produce anxiety, fear, distrust, panic, or other unwanted psychological reactions in some people. Anyone using weed alongside prescription medication, or attempting to manage persistent pain, sleep problems, or psychiatric symptoms, should discuss cannabis use with an appropriate healthcare professional rather than treating the strain description as medical guidance.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Critical Auto stays close to a traditional citrus-and-pine cannabis profile. Fast Buds describes lemon, citrus, and pine as the central flavors, backed by earth and a persistent floral quality on the exhale. Freshly broken flowers may release lemon peel first, followed by dry pine needles and a darker soil-like foundation. The floral component becomes more noticeable behind the citrus, preventing the aroma from turning entirely sharp or resinous. Compared with modern candy, sherbet, and pastry hybrids, the profile feels distinctly old-school.

Fast Buds does not currently publish a laboratory table assigning individual terpene compounds and percentages to this cultivar. For that reason, presenting a fixed myrcene, limonene, caryophyllene, or pinene ranking would go beyond the breeder data. What can be stated confidently is the sensory direction documented by Fast Buds: lemon and citrus brightness layered over pine, flowers, and earth. Phenotype, light intensity, harvest timing, drying conditions, curing, and storage can all influence how strongly those aromatic qualities survive in finished cannabis.
Growing Information

Yield is the plant’s headline cultivation trait. Fast Buds’ detailed grow guide lists approximately 350–550 g/m² indoors and 50–150 g per outdoor plant, while promotional descriptions note that optimized indoor crops can approach 600 g/m². Plants generally reach about 90–120 cm, making them relatively large for an automatic strain but still manageable in most indoor environments. The full life cycle is approximately ten weeks, although individual documented grows have extended into an eleventh week before harvest.

Structurally, short internodal spacing allows dense buds to form repeatedly along the branches. Outdoors, Fast Buds describes a Christmas-tree growth pattern, especially in warm Mediterranean-style climates, while indoor plants develop enough mass that branches may require physical support. The flowers themselves are compact and heavy, with swollen calyxes, golden pistils, and abundant resin. Fast Buds specifically recommends bamboo stakes or trellising because late-flowering colas can become too heavy for unsupported branches.

Its resilience makes Critical Auto particularly accessible to beginners. The breeder describes it as resistant, reliable, and capable of performing across a broad range of conditions, with especially strong outdoor results in warm climates. Gentle early training can spread flowering sites and control height, but autos have limited time to recover from severe stress because flowering begins regardless of plant size. Consistent irrigation, healthy root development , strong light, and adequate late-flower airflow are therefore more useful than overly aggressive manipulation.
FAQ
Is Critical Auto indica or sativa?

Fast Buds classifies Critical Auto as 60% indica and 40% sativa. The physical side is relaxing, but the cultivar retains enough cerebral energy to produce creative, happy, and motivated effects at moderate doses.
What are the genetics of Critical Auto?

Fast Buds describes it as its improved autoflowering version of Critical Mass. The current breeder specification lists the genetics as “Critical Autoflower” but does not publicly name the exact automatic parent, so a more specific parental formula should not be assumed.
How strong is Critical Auto?

Fast Buds’ detailed cultivation guide lists THC at up to approximately 20%, with CBD below 1%. Actual cannabinoid levels can vary according to phenotype, growing environment, harvest maturity, drying, and curing.
How long does Critical Auto take from seed to harvest?
The breeder gives approximately ten weeks for the complete cycle. Some real-world grows can extend closer to eleven weeks, particularly when plants need additional time to reach full flower maturity.
How much does Critical Auto yield?
Fast Buds lists approximately 350–550 g/m² indoors and 50–150 g per plant outdoors in its detailed cultivation material. The breeder also promotes optimized indoor production reaching about 600 g/m².
Final Thoughts on Critical Auto

Critical Auto earns its reputation through productivity rather than novelty. Fast Buds has taken Critical Mass-style cannabis and developed an automatic line that combines dense flower formation, substantial resin, an approximately ten-week life cycle, and indoor yields capable of exceeding half a kilogram per square meter under favorable conditions. Its lemon, pine, floral, and earthy character keeps the finished flower rooted in traditional marijuana flavor rather than following modern dessert trends.

The effect is equally balanced: physical relaxation develops quickly, yet creativity and mental engagement can remain intact before heavier consumption pushes the experience toward a dreamier state. For growers, easy cultivation, sturdy genetics, strong outdoor performance, and unusually heavy colas make the plant particularly practical. Because several breeders market their own Critical autos, keeping the Fast Buds designation attached to these figures is essential. Within that specific line, Critical Auto stands out as a high-yielding, forgiving, old-school-flavored autoflower built around straightforward performance.
